title: Vegetable Cornish Pasty
subtitle: A crimped shortcrust pasty filled with potato, swede, leek and carrot
excerpt: A proper crimped pasty with a dense filling of raw vegetables cooked inside the shortcrust case. Sturdy enough to carry as a packed lunch.
sourceNotes: Inspired by the traditional Cornish pasty method with raw vegetables sealed inside the pastry.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze baked pasties individually. Reheat from frozen at 180C for 30 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Scale up the filling easily. Roll and fill one pasty at a time to keep the pastry cold.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble and chill overnight. Glaze and bake the next day.

content.text: The vegetables go in raw and cook inside the sealed pastry case. Slice them very thin so they are tender by the time the pastry is done. A firm crimp all the way round stops steam from splitting the sides.

items.prepNote: white and pale green part, finely sliced

content.text: Mix the potato, swede, carrot and leek together in a bowl. Season well with salt and pepper.
Divide the pastry into four equal pieces. On a lightly floured surface, roll each piece into a circle about 22cm across.
Pile a quarter of the vegetable mix onto one half of each circle, leaving a 2cm border. Dot a few pieces of butter over the top.
Brush the border with beaten egg. Fold the pastry over and press the edges together firmly. Crimp by folding and twisting the edge in a rope pattern.
Place on the lined tray and chill for 20 minutes. Heat the oven to 200C.
Brush all over with beaten egg. Cut a small slit in the top of each pasty to let steam out.
Bake for 55 minutes until golden and the vegetables feel tender through the slit. Rest for 10 minutes before eating.

items.symptom: The vegetables are still hard inside.
items.cause: The slices were too thick or the oven temperature was too low.
items.fix: Slice the vegetables as thin as possible, no more than 2mm. Check the oven temperature with a thermometer.

items.cause: The seal was not pressed firmly enough before crimping.
items.fix: Press the edges together with your fingers first, then crimp. Work around the whole edge without rushing.

items.symptom: The base is pale and soft.
items.cause: The baking tray was cold when the pasties went in.
items.fix: Preheat the baking tray in the oven for 10 minutes before adding the pasties.
